Nothing selected.
Pick a configuration file from the left.
Start from what you want to do. Each guided workflow picks the right configuration file(s) and composes names from the naming convention — no manual file or column knowledge required. Nothing is written to disk until Commit all on the Review & Save tab.
1 Direct — who gets access A named admin becomes a member of a direct group. That membership is the access.
👤

Assign an administrator

Provision a privileged account for a new administrator and make it a member of one or more direct groups. This is how a person actually gets access.
👥

Create or update a direct group

The group people are members of — scoped to a role and one organisational dimension (department, org, project or cross-org, whichever your organisation uses). Nests the permission groups that give it its capabilities.
⌚

Time-boxed project access

A direct group plus its members and a fixed end date, in one pass. Defaults to 90 days. Use this instead of 1 + 2 when the access is temporary.
2 Indirect — what that access can do A direct group is nested into permission groups. Those hold the actual Entra roles, Azure RBAC and workload permissions.
→

Delegate a permission

Start here. Target-first: pick what you are delegating — Entra ID, an Azure scope, or a workload — and the role(s). The engine derives the group name, level, tier and plane, and can nest it into direct groups in the same pass.
+

Permission group — Entra IDadvanced

Build the Entra ID capability bundle directly, without the target-first flow. Use when you already know the group you want.
+

Permission group — Azure resourceadvanced

Build the Azure RBAC capability bundle directly, at a chosen management group, subscription or resource group scope.
⎘ Utilities Shortcuts over the two layers above.
⎘

Duplicate an existing group

Use any direct group or permission group as a template, assign a new short code, and adjust before committing.

Permission Templates

Centrally maintained delegation packs. When a template gains new roles (e.g. Defender XDR grew from 3 to 7), the new rows show here for one-click import into pending.

Backups & undo

Every commit takes a timestamped backup before it writes. A failed commit rolls back automatically; below you can also undo a completed commit by restoring an earlier snapshot. The newest backups are kept (oldest are pruned).
